docs.title: Index management
docs.text:
[POST] /Lucene/createindex/{index}

Creates an index named {index}

[DELETE] /Lucene/removeindex/{index}

Permanently deletes the index

[GET] /Lucene/indexexists/{index}

Checks whether an index exists.

[POST] /Lucene/refresh/{index}

Leads to a refresh of the listed index. This ensures that after adding documents, you can search for the newly indexed documents. Using the .NET client this call is made automatically when the client is unloaded (Dispose()).

[POST] /Lucene/releaseall

Releases all shared resources within the server. For example, the IndexReader or IndexWriter, which are shared across multiple queries in the server for optimal performance. After releasing, the resources are reinitialized the next time you access an index. This call is mainly necessary for development and should not be necessary in a productive environment.

docs.title: Mapping
docs.text:
This determines the structure of the documents for this index. The Mapping specifies which fields the documents can have for this index and whether they are indexed or are only additional information (without search options).

[POST] /Lucene/map/{index}

Request Body

{
  "fields": [
    {
      "fieldType": "string",
      "name": "string",
      "store": true,
      "index": true
    }
  ],
  "primaryFields": [
    "string"
  ]
}

A Json File is passed in which each field is defined. Values for 'fieldType' are:

  • guid: creates a field (_guid) for which an id is automatically generated. this id can be used to explicitly search for or delete a document

  • text: The field contains text that is indexed. Fields of this type can search for keywords or word fragments.

  • string: A string to search for.

  • int32, single, double: Integer or floating point numbers

  • datetime: A date with time

  • geo: Geometry (e.B latitude and longitude)

For each field, you can specify whether it should be indexed and/or saved. You can search for indexed fields. For saved fields, the content is also returned 1:n on a hit.

primaryFields must specify an array of column names in which a search should be searched by default. All other fields are searched only if explicitly stated in the query.

[GET] /Lucene/mapping/{index}

Here you can query the mapping for this index. The result is again an IApiResult object with an additional property mapping:

{
  "mapping": {
    "fields": [
      {
        "fieldType": "guid",
        "name": "_guid",
        "store": true,
        "index": true
      },
      ...
    ],
    "primaryFields": [
      "title",
      "content"
    ],
    "primaryFieldsEncodeCharacters":[".","/"], // optional
    "primaryFieldsPhonetics": 200  // optional
  },
  "success": true,
  "milliSeconds": 12.2342
}

primaryFields are fields in which searches are made default, if no explicit fields are specified in the query.

Additional methods could be used for the primary fields, that improve search behavior:

Lucene uses characters such as . or / as delimiters and they are not included in queries. However, certain data may require you to search for these characters. For example, property number in this form is: .432/12. To ensure this, a trick can be used in which these characters are replaced before indexing to a (pseudo) ASCII value. Then, Lucene no longer recognizes them as separators. This behavior can be controlled through the primaryFieldsEncodeCharacters property. The ASCII encoding then takes place automatically in the background when indexing and searching documents.

If you also want to be able to search "phonetically" in the index, the property primaryFieldsPhonetics must be set. The code given here determines: which algorithm to use for phonetic search. The algorithm is defined by one of the following values:

public enum Algorithm
{
    None = 0,               // default
    Soundex = 100,          // for english text
    ColognePhonetics = 200, // ideal for german text
    ColognePhonetics_with_doubles = 201,
    ColognePhonetics_clean_zero = 202,  
}

docs.title: Custom metadata
docs.text:
Any text (e.g. JSON) can be stored with an index under a name. Names follow the same rules as index names; mapping is reserved.

[POST] /Lucene/addmeta/{index}?name={name}

Request body:

{ "metadata": "any string, e.g. serialized JSON" }

[GET] /Lucene/getmeta/{index}?name={name}

Returns the metadata stored under name (attribute metadata).

[GET] /Lucene/getmetas/{index}

Returns all metadata of the index as a dictionary name -> metadata.

[GET] /Lucene/getmetanames/{index}

Returns the names of all metadata entries (attribute result).

docs.title: Documents
docs.text:
An entry in the index is called a document. Documents can be indexed, queried, and deleted using the following interfaces. If new documents are added to or deleted to an index, this will only become visible after a refresh (see above).

[POST] /Lucene/index/{index}

This allows individual documents to be transferred to the index. The fields of the documents passed must correspond to the Mapping. Unmapped fields are ignored.

Request Body

[
  {   
      // any kind of properties
      "title": "my book title",
      "summary": "lorem ispum..."
  }
]

[DELETE] /Lucene/remove/{index}?term={query-term}&termField={optional:field-used-for-term}

A query can be passed as term. The criteria from the query are searched in termField and the corresponding objects are deleted.

The Default value for termField is _guid. Ideally, in the Mapping you specify a field with the type guid. This is the only way to delete individual documents.

[GET] /Lucene/search/{index}?q={query-term}&outFields={optional:fields-for-the-result-comma-separated}&filter={geo-filter}&format={output-format}

This method can be used to search for documents. The result is of type IApiResult with an additional hits attributes:

Example: /Lucene/search/{index}?q=rules /Lucene/search/{index}?q=rules&outFields=_guid,title,publish_date

{
  "hits": [
    {
      "_score": 1.4272848,
      "_guid": "256c3f501ef64327b81f4b8141a6f5ef",
      "title": "LuceneServerNET rules!",
      "publish_date": "2021-02-12T17:09:17"
    }
  ],
  "success": true,
  "milliSeconds": 1.8725
}

Paging: optional parameters from (offset, default 0; from + size max. 10000), size (default 20) and searchAfter (cursor). The response additionally contains totalHits, from, size and nextSearchAfter, see API v2 – Search and paging.

The Query-Term corresponds to the Lucene syntax, see also here

Functions can also be applied to the outFields, for example, to return only a certain amount of characters. That one makes sense when very large documents are indexed and not always the complete content of the documents should be returned. If outField functions are used, a semicolon (;) must be used as a separator between each value. If only one field is passed, the statement must be completed with a semicolon.

Functions are appended to a field with a .. Several functions can also be specified in a chain:

content.WORDS(10).AS("new_field_name"); content.SENTENCES_WITH("batman robin", 2, 2);content.INCL("batman robin").AS("incl");

The following functions are available:

  • CHARS([int]number): Returns the specified number of characters
  • WORDS([int]number): Returns the specified number of words
  • SENTENCES_WITH("[string]terms", [int]takeHits, [int]takeDefaults): Returns only sentences containing at least one of the keywords listed. terms are the keywords separated by a space. takeHits indicates the maximum number of sentences will return. takeDefaults - if no hits are found, the number of first n-sentences specified here is returned instead.
  • INCL("[string]terms"): returns the keywords that actually exist in the field value. Separators are spaces here again
  • AS("[string]name"): Renames the field in the result. This makes sense if a field should be returned multiple times, e.g. once as original and once only with the keywords included.

The filter (geo-filter) can be used to restrict the search geographically. To do this, a geo field must be defined via the mapping. Possible filter calls can be as follows:

filter=bbox({geo-field-name}:15.01,47.01,15.03,47.03) In addition to the name of the geo field, the coordinates of the BoundingBox are specified (minX,minY,maxX,maxY).

filter=dist_km({geo-field-name}:15.01,47.01,0.3) Filters results within x kilometers (x,y,distance[km])

filter=linedist_km({geo-field-name}:15.43682,47.06630,15.44682,47.07830,15.45682,47.06630,0.01) (x1,y1,x2,y2,...dist[km])

An output format can be determined via the Format. The output is usually always a JSON format. If the results have a stored geo field (must be mapped as stored), the results can also be output as GeoJSON. This makes it easier to integrate the results to an existing GI applications:

format={geo-fieldname}:geojson

[GET] /Lucene/searchphonetic/{index}?q={term}&outFields={optional:fields-for-the-result-comma-separated}&filter={geo-filter}&format={output-format}

Like search with the difference that here a phonetically searched in performed in the primary fields. Here no query but the search term is passed. No query syntax may be passed as with search! The conversion of the term into a query takes place here under hood.

[GET] /Lucene/group/{index}?groupField={field}&q={optional:query-term}

This method can be used to determine possible values of a field that optionally correspond to a query term. The method is similar to a DISTINCT in a database. The hits are a objects with the value (value) and the number of hits (_hits).

Example: /Lucene/group/{index}?groupField=feed

{
  "hits": [
    {
      "value": "heise",
      "_hits": 564
    },
    {
      "value": "derstandard",
      "_hits": 1119
    },
    {
      "value": "kurier",
      "_hits": 183
    },
    {
      "value": "diepresse",
      "_hits": 393
    },
    {
      "value": "krone",
      "_hits": 493
    },
    {
      "value": "futurezone",
      "_hits": 140
    }
  ],
  "success": true,
  "milliSeconds": 358.4401
}

docs.title: Changelog
docs.text:
All notable changes to LuceneServerNET are documented in this file.

The format is based on Keep a Changelog.

docs.title: Migration from 2.x
docs.text: Area What changes What to do Index ids / metadata names Only a-z, 0-9, _, -, max. 64 chars Rename index folders that do not match before upgrading HTTP methods createindex, refresh, releaseall → POST; removeindex, remove → DELETE Update REST clients; old GET routes work while LuceneServer:AllowLegacyGetMutations is true (default) – set it to false once all clients are migrated NuGet LuceneServerNET.Client 3.0.0 Uses POST/DELETE Requires a v3 server – upgrade the server first Authentication Roles read/write/admin, hashed secrets (SecretHash) Not breaking: clients without Roles get admin, plain Secret still works. Recommended: assign roles and switch to SecretHash (--hash-secret) API v2 errors HTTP 4xx/5xx instead of 200 Only relevant for new v2 clients; v1 is unchanged Swagger Replaced by /openapi/{v}.json and /scalar Old /swagger URLs redirect Phonetic search Fixed Cologne phonetics and Soundex codes (see Fixed) Recommended: re-index indices with primaryFieldsPhonetics, otherwise affected words do not match in searchphonetic until re-indexed. Normal search is not affected .NET client dispose Console output replaced by optional Logger; IAsyncDisposable Not breaking. Optionally use await using; set Logger to keep the refresh log lines datetime fields Values without time zone are taken as UTC (before: server local time); results contain Z Only relevant if the server does not run in UTC and clients send dates without time zone: send Z/an offset or re-index. Docker (UTC) is not affected Versions Server, Engine, Core and Client share one version (git tag v*, MinVer) –

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• Docker image and Aspire AppHost no longer set LuceneServer:ArchivePath (the archive is optional, set it explicitly if needed).
  • PUT /api/v2/indices/{index}?archive=false creates an index without archive (also with ArchivePath); client CreateIndexAsync(index, archive: false). Import jobs create their index generations without archive (about 26 times faster on Windows).

  • DELETE /api/v2/indices/{index}/meta/{name} removes a custom metadata entry (also from the archive); client RemoveMetadataAsync.

  • REST API v2 (/api/v2/indices/{id}/...), resource oriented, in parallel to v1 (/Lucene/...). v1 stays fully supported (not breaking) but is marked as deprecated in Swagger. Separate OpenAPI documents for v1 and v2.

  • Paging and total hit count for search (v1 and v2, additive): new optional parameters from (offset, from + size ≤ 10000) and searchAfter (cursor); responses contain totalHits, from, size and nextSearchAfter.
  • LuceneServerNET.Client: SearchPageAsync / SearchPhoneticPageAsync (existing methods unchanged).
  • Index aliases (additive): an alias points to one index and can be used instead of the index id in all v1 and v2 endpoints (search, documents, mapping, metadata, stats, export), except creating and removing indices. Switching is atomic, e.g. rebuild into orte_20261107 and switch the alias orte without downtime. GET /api/v2/aliases, PUT /api/v2/aliases/{alias} ({ "index": "..." }, role write), DELETE /api/v2/aliases/{alias}. Stored in {RootPath}/aliases.json (copy in {ArchivePath}). An index used by an alias can not be removed (409), an alias can not have the name of an index. Client: GetAliasesAsync, SetAliasAsync, RemoveAliasAsync.
  • Admin UI (LuceneServerNET.Admin, Blazor Server + MudBlazor), a separate web app that administrates several server instances through the v2 API: dashboard (health, version, uptime, roles), index list with document count and size, search playground (autocomplete, search with paging/sort/spatial filter, phonetic search, group by, curl command), create index with mapping editor, import from CSV/JSON (mapping proposed from a sample, configurable batch size, error report, cancel), metadata editor and maintenance (refresh, delete documents by query, clear, delete index). Login: local users (hashed passwords, --hash-password) or OpenID Connect. Instances from the configuration and added in the UI (secrets encrypted with DataProtection, SQLite/Dapper). Docker image: Dockerfile.admin; started by the Aspire AppHost. Import from a database (SQL Server, PostgreSQL, SQLite): stored connections (encrypted), a SELECT query with preview, then the same mapping proposal and batch import as for files. Geo data import: geometry columns (WKB/EWKB, WKT/EWKT, GeoJSON; PostGIS ST_AsEWKB, SQL Server STAsBinary()), GeoJSON files (FeatureCollection) and coordinate columns (lat/lon, x/y), converted to WGS84 with Proj4Net (source EPSG from the SRID of the value or chosen in the UI). Lines/polygons are indexed as point on surface plus a bounding box field (<field>_bbox), the original geometry can be stored as GeoJSON (<field>_geojson). PostGIS geometry / geography columns are read directly (also with SELECT *), SQL Server geometry columns give a hint to use STAsBinary(). Encoded characters of the primary fields (PrimaryFieldsEncodeCharacters, e.g. ./) can be set when creating an index, importing and in import jobs. Template fields in the import mapping: a field built from columns ({PLZ} {ORT} {STR} {HNR}, empty brackets removed), with text replacements. Database connections: show the stored connection string on request with masked password (audit log), edit it without re-entering the password; connection test in the list. Copy an index (mapping, metadata, documents) to another name or another instance. Alias management. Scheduled import jobs (cron, time zone) from a database query: rebuild a new index generation and switch an alias (no downtime, keeps N older generations, a failed run leaves the alias unchanged), clear and refill or append; run history, run now, cancel; dry run (read and convert only) and time per phase (read, convert, send) in the run history; live progress of running jobs (rows, rate, estimate from the last run); manual jobs without schedule; missed runs are caught up once at startup (per job); several sources per job (one index, metadata entry per source with a stable meta id, template variables {@metaid}/{@category}); "webgis" template (id, suggested_text, subtext, category, thumbnail_url, geo, bbox) replacing gView FillLuceneServer; import of gView FillLuceneServer configurations as job; external trigger per job (POST /api/jobs/{id}/run with a job token, e.g. from Jenkins; a trigger during a run queues one more run; status via GET /api/jobs/{id}/runs/{runId}, optional note); optional webhook after a run (always or on failure, JSON statistics with a Slack/Mattermost compatible text, encrypted header, 3 attempts). Admin UI as Windows service: lucene-admin-service.bat install|uninstall [name] [port] (virtual service account, restart on failure, data and configuration _config/admin.json next to the version folders, event log); the win64 release ZIP contains the admin UI ({version}/admin) and the scripts. IIS notes for import jobs in the docs. Index backup as ZIP download (manifest, mapping, metadata, documents as NDJSON) and restore from such a ZIP. Audit log of all changing actions (index, mapping/metadata, import, instances, connections, login), with filter page and retention (Admin:Audit:RetentionDays, default 180).
  • API v2 endpoints for administration: GET /api/v2/indices (index names), GET /api/v2/indices/{id}/stats (documents, size on disk, last modification), GET /api/v2/admin/info (version, uptime, platform; role admin) and GET /api/v2/admin/whoami (roles of the calling client) and GET /api/v2/indices/{id}/documents/_export (all documents as NDJSON, stored fields; role read).
  • LuceneServerNET.Client: new LuceneServerV2Client for the v2 API (not bound to one index; LuceneServerClient is unchanged), incl. ExportDocumentsAsync (streamed).

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• Engine: errors of the background refresh/commit and of releasing indices are logged via ILogger (before: Console.Error), so they show up in structured logs / OpenTelemetry.

  • New config LuceneServer:BackgroundCommitSeconds (default 20): interval of the background refresh + commit of all open indices.

  • LuceneServerNET.Client: refresh on dispose made configurable and safer (not breaking):

  • New property RefreshChangedIndicesOnDispose (default true = previous behavior).
  • Implements IAsyncDisposable; use await using. Dispose() still works and no longer blocks on async code in the caller's synchronization context; it is idempotent and never throws.
  • No more Console.WriteLine output; optional Logger property (ILogger) instead. cmd/ImportDbTable passes a console logger.
  • Without a passed HttpClient, all instances share one internal HttpClient instead of creating (and never disposing) one per instance.

  • New dependencies: Microsoft.Bcl.AsyncInterfaces, Microsoft.Extensions.Logging.Abstractions.

  • Error handling: errors are logged only via ILogger (no more Console.WriteLine), milliSeconds is measured with Stopwatch.

  • New config LuceneServer:MaxRequestBodySizeBytes (default 30 MB, Kestrel and IIS) limits request bodies, e.g. for indexing.
  • New config LuceneServer:UseHttpsRedirection (default false) enables HTTP → HTTPS redirection.

  • A warning is logged if the OpenAPI/Scalar UI is enabled outside Development (useSwagger: true).

  • OpenAPI via Microsoft.AspNetCore.OpenApi and Scalar instead of Swashbuckle. ASP.NET Core no longer ships Swagger by default; the documents are now generated by the framework (OpenAPI 3.1). Swashbuckle is removed.

  • Documents: /openapi/v1.json, /openapi/v2.json; UI: /scalar (Basic auth supported in "Try it").
  • Old URLs /swagger and /swagger/{v}/swagger.json redirect to the new ones.
  • Config key useSwagger is unchanged.

docs.title: Changed (breaking)
docs.text:
• API v2 returns errors with HTTP status codes instead of HTTP 200: 400 (invalid query/ParseException, invalid filter, invalid parameters such as from + size > 10000), 404 (index not found), 409 (index already exists / is unloading), 500 (other errors). The body is still {"success": false, "message": "..."}. v1 (/Lucene/...) is unchanged and keeps HTTP 200. For client errors (4xx) the message is now returned also in production (before: only the exception type).

  • State-changing endpoints no longer use HTTP GET. GET requests must be safe; prefetchers, link previews, crawlers and CSRF (<img src=…>) could create or delete indices.

  • POST /Lucene/createindex/{id}, DELETE /Lucene/removeindex/{id}, DELETE /Lucene/remove/{id}?term=…&termField=…, POST /Lucene/refresh/{id}, POST /Lucene/releaseall.
  • Transition: the old GET routes still work while LuceneServer:AllowLegacyGetMutations is true (default). They are marked [Obsolete], return Deprecation: true and Warning: 299 headers and log a warning. With false they return 405 Method Not Allowed.
  • LuceneServerNET.Client 3.0.0 uses the new methods and therefore requires a v3 server.

docs.title: Security
docs.text:
• Path traversal protection for index and metadata names. Index ids from the route (e.g. removeindex/..) and custom metadata names (e.g. getmeta/{id}?name=../../x) were passed unchecked into Path.Combine and could read, create or delete files and directories outside of RootPath / ArchivePath.
  • Index ids and metadata names must now match ^[a-z0-9_-]{1,64}$ (ids are lower-cased first).
  • Validation happens centrally in the controller and again in the engine (LuceneService, LuceneSharedResourcesService, ArchiveService).
  • All file system paths are built via the new PathGuard.Combine, which ensures the resolved path stays below the configured root directory.
  • releaseall no longer uses the "*" placeholder id; every route id is validated without exception.

docs.title: Breaking Changes
docs.text:
• Index ids and metadata names containing characters other than a-z, 0-9, _, - (e.g. ., spaces, umlauts) or longer than 64 characters are now rejected.
  • REST clients: such requests return an error result (success: false).
  • NuGet client LuceneServerNET.Client: no API change; affected calls receive the error result.
  • Existing indices on disk: files are not touched, but indices whose folder name does not match the rule are no longer reachable via the API until renamed.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• Numbers independent of the server culture: stored double/single/int32 values were returned formatted with the server culture ("47,0707" on a german server) and numeric strings in documents were parsed with it ("47.0707" was indexed as 470707). Values are now parsed and returned culture invariant ("47.0707"; still as string, like before). Stored-only numeric fields (index: false) also accept JSON values now. Indices with numeric strings indexed on a non-english server should be re-indexed.
  • datetime independent of the server time zone: dates without time zone were interpreted as server local time and shifted to UTC (1128-01-01 became 1127-12-31T23:00:00 on a server in CET) and were returned without Z. Now: values without time zone are UTC, values with Z/offset are converted, results are UTC with Z. Stored-only date fields are written as ISO 8601 (older culture formatted values are still read).

  • group: group values are decoded with BytesRef.Utf8ToString() (respects offset/length) instead of decoding the whole underlying byte buffer. No visible effect with the current Lucene.NET version (it returns exact copies), but no longer relies on that implementation detail.

  • Cologne phonetics: a c at the end of a word was ignored; it is now encoded as 8 (Novac → 638, before 63).

  • Soundex: the code of the first letter is now used to suppress an identical following code (Pfister → P236, before P123), and vowels now separate identical codes while h/w do not (Tymczak → T522, before T520).

  • ⚠️ Both fixes change the stored phonetic codes. Existing indices keep the old codes until they are re-indexed: e.g. a misspelled search for Nowac no longer finds Novac via searchphonetic until the index is rebuilt. Only the phonetic fields are affected, not the normal search.

  • GeoPoint(latitude, longitude) constructor set Latitude twice; Longidute stayed 0.

  • GeoType.Parse never parsed coordinate strings (inverted IsNullOrEmpty check). Strings are now read as "lon lat" or "lon,lat" (same order as GeoPoint.ToString()); invalid strings are ignored instead of throwing.

  • The reserved metadata name mapping is now actually blocked (the old check compared against "mapping " with a trailing space).

docs.title: Tools
docs.text:
The cmd/ folder contains two console applications that use the .NET client. Build them with dotnet publish cmd/CreateIndex or dotnet publish cmd/ImportDbTable.

Note

If the server requires authentication, pass the credentials in the server URL: -s https://importer:my-secret@search.example.com.

docs.title: CreateIndex
docs.text:
Creates an index and its mapping.

CreateIndex -server[-s] server
            -index[-i] indexname
            -field[-f] fieldname[.fieldtype][.stored|not_stored]   // indexed field, default .text.stored
            -sfield fieldname[.fieldtype]                          // stored only field, default .text
            -primary field1,field2                                 // primary search fields, default: first field
            -remove                                                // remove an existing index first

Field types: text, string, int32, single, double, datetime, geo, guid.

.\CreateIndex.exe -s https://localhost:44393 `
                  -i new-index `
                  -f suggested_text `
                  -f sub_text `
                  -f category `
                  -sfield id

docs.title: ImportDbTable
docs.text:
Reads rows from a database and indexes them (in batches of 1000).

ImportDbTable -server[-s] {server}
              -index[-i] {indexname}
              -db-type {PostGres|Oracle|SqlServer|Sqlite}
              -db-connectionstring[-db] {connectionString}
              -sql-statement[-sql] {sqlStatement}
              -f {indexfield} {expression}     // expression: "lorem {{DB_FIELD1}} ipsum {{DB_FIELD2}}"

Each -f maps an index field to an expression; {{COLUMN}} is replaced with the column value.

.\ImportDbTable.exe -s https://localhost:44393 -i addresses `
    -db-type SqlServer `
    -db "Server=.;Database=gis;Trusted_Connection=True" `
    -sql "SELECT id, street, nr, city FROM addresses" `
    -f suggested_text "{{street}} {{nr}}" `
    -f sub_text "{{city}}" `
    -f id "{{id}}"

The index must exist and be mapped first (e.g. with CreateIndex).

docs.title: .NET client
docs.text:
The LuceneServerClient class is part of a .NET Standard library and provides easy access to the REST API of LuceneServer.NET.

The class is in the LuceneServerNET.Client.dll and can be added to existing projects via nuget.org. The source code is also included in this repository.

docs.title: Instantiation
docs.text:
A client can be instantiated as follows:

await using (var client = new LuceneServerClient(serverUrl, indexName))
{
    // client operations
}

A client always refers to one index. The corresponding index can be specified via the indexName.

docs.title: Refresh and Dispose
docs.text:
New or removed documents are not immediately visible to searches. The server makes them visible and writes them to disk (commit) on a refresh. This happens

  • explicitly via await client.RefreshIndex(),
  • automatically in the background on the server within about 20 seconds,
  • when the server shuts down normally.

If documents were indexed or removed with a client and no RefreshIndex() followed, the client refreshes the index when it is disposed. Changes are then visible immediately after the using block, e.g. for an import tool that searches right afterwards or exits. If the client is used only for querying, using can be omitted.

  • Use await using (DisposeAsync()) in async code. The synchronous Dispose() is still supported.
  • Errors during this refresh are not thrown (the server commits in the background anyway); they are written to the optional Logger.
  • The refresh on dispose can be switched off, e.g. for a web application that makes many small changes and can live with the short delay:
await using (var client = new LuceneServerClient(serverUrl, indexName)
{
    RefreshChangedIndicesOnDispose = false,   // default: true
    Logger = loggerFactory.CreateLogger<LuceneServerClient>()  // optional, default: no logging
})
{
    // client operations
}

docs.title: HttpClient
docs.text:
To communicate with the LuceneServerNET, the client uses a System.Net.Http.HttpClient. If none is passed, all client instances share one internal HttpClient (creating one per instance can exhaust sockets). An existing HttpClient (e.g. from IHttpClientFactory) can be passed as an additional parameter:

await using (var client = new LuceneServerClient(serverUrl, indexName, myHttpClient))
{
    // client operations
}

This ensures that, for example, Authorization headers set on that HttpClient are passed to the server. A passed HttpClient is not disposed by the client.

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text:
If the server requires Basic authentication, pass the client id and secret:

using(var client = new LuceneServerClient(serverUrl, indexName, "importer", "my-secret"))
{
    // client operations
}

Alternatively the credentials can be part of the URL: https://importer:my-secret@search.example.com.

docs.title: Methods
docs.text:
The following methods are used for index management:

// Check if index exists
if (await client.IndexExistsAsync())
{
    // if true: remove existing index
    await client.RemoveIndexAsync();
}
// create a new index
await client.CreateIndexAsync();

To map an index, a MappingIndex object must first be created. This then specifies the fields and primary search fields. The MapAsync function sets the mapping for the index:

var mapping = new IndexMapping()
{
    // primary search field for the index
    PrimaryFields = new string[] { "title", "content" },
    Fields = new FieldMapping[]
    {
        //  create _guid field, so that documents can be queried or deleted individually
        new DocumentGuidField(),
        // Indexed (queryable) fields, default-type: FieldTypes.TextType
        new IndexField("title"),
        new IndexField("content"),
        new IndexField("feed_id", FieldTypes.StringType),
        new IndexField("publish_date", FieldTypes.DateTimeType),
        // stored (not queryable) fields
        new StoredField("url"),
        new StoredField("image"),
    }
};

// Map
await client.MapAsync(mapping);

To index documents, they must be passed to the client as IEnumerable<IDictionary<string, object>>. A value for the DocumentGuid field _guid is not passed here, but is set automatically by the server.

var doc = new Dictionary<string, object>();

doc["title"] = "My Documents Title";
doc["content"] = "Lorem Ipsum...";
doc["feed_id"] = "an_id_for_my_feed";
doc["publish_date"] = DateTime.Now;
doc["url"] = "https://my-article.com";
doc["image"] = "https://my-article.com/preview.jpg";

await client.IndexDocumentsAsync(new IDictionary<string, object>[] {
    doc
});

The following methods can be used to delete documents:

// delete by _guid: Task<bool> RemoveDocumentsAsync(IEnumerable<Guid> guids)
await client.RemoveDocumentsAsync(new Guid[] { guid_doc1, guid_doc2 /*, ...*/  });

// delete by query term: Task<bool> RemoveDocumentsAsync(string field, string term)
await client.RemoveDocumentsAsync("title", "Batman");  // title contains Batman

The search is implemented in the function Task<LuceneSearchResult> SearchAsync(string query, IEnumerable<string> outFields = null). The Query syntax is the same as that of Lucene. Examples can be found here

Primary searches in the fields listed in the mapping. However, the Query syntax can also be used to search in all other indexed fields.

For simple full-text searches where the user enters keywords, it is recommended to adjust the input:

Input: Batm Robi

Query: +Batm* +Robi* => both search terms must occur (+), search with wildcard => all documents containing Batman and Robin are found.

The QueryBuilder class can be used to convert to this syntax:

var queryBuilder = new QueryBuilder();
var result = await client.SearchAsync($"{ queryBuilder.ParseTerm(term) }");

return result.Hits;

In addition to the term, you can specify the fields that should be returned. For the outfields also special functions are available, see the REST API.

var result = await client.SearchAsync(term,
                                      outFields: new[]
                                      {
                                        "*",  // all fields
                                        "content".SentencesWith("batman robin",1,1),
                                        "content".IncludedTerms("batman robin").As("incl")
                                      },
                                      size: 50,
                                      sortField: "publish_date",
                                      sortReverse: true);

docs.title: Custom metadata
docs.text:
await client.AddCustomMetadataAsync("source", "{ \"db\": \"products\" }");
var meta = await client.GetCustomMetadataAsync("source");
var names = await client.GetCustomMetadataNamesAsync();
var all = await client.GetCustomMetadatasAsync();

docs.title: Phonetic search and grouping
docs.text:
// phonetic search in the primary fields (no query syntax, plain term)
var result = await client.SearchPhoneticAsync("meier");

// distinct values of a field
var groups = await client.GroupAsync("feed_id");

docs.title: Sample applications
docs.text: The repository contains two small sample applications in the test/ folder. Both expect a server at https://localhost:44393; adjust the URL in the source code.

docs.title: ConsoleClient
docs.text:
test/ConsoleClient reads RSS feeds and shows how to

  • create and map an index (CreateIndex()),
  • index documents in batches (IndexItems()),
  • group values of a field (Group()).
dotnet run --project test/ConsoleClient

docs.title: WebClient
docs.text:
test/WebClient is an ASP.NET Core Razor Pages app with an autocomplete search box. The page handler converts the user input with QueryBuilder.ParseTerm() and calls SearchAsync():

var result = await _client.SearchAsync($"{ new QueryBuilder().ParseTerm(term) }");

dotnet run --project test/WebClient

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
The server reads the standard ASP.NET Core configuration sources (appsettings.json, environment variables, command line) plus the file _config/luceneserver.json. The file is created on the first start (see Installation).

{
  "LuceneServer": {
    "RootPath": "c:\\data\\lucene\\indices",
    "ArchivePath": "c:\\data\\lucene\\archive",
    "AutoRestoreOnStartup": true,
    "AutoRestoreOnStartupCount": 0,
    "AutoRestoreOnStartupSinceSeconds": 86400,
    "MaxRequestBodySizeBytes": 31457280,
    "UseHttpsRedirection": false
  },
  "useSwagger": false,
  "Authorization": {
    "Type": "Basic",
    "Clients": [ ]
  }
}

Tip

The template uses keys with a trailing underscore (ArchivePath_, Authorization_). These are ignored. Remove the underscore to activate a section.

docs.title: LuceneServer
docs.text: Key Description RootPath Directory containing the index folders. Required. ArchivePath Optional, not set by default. If set, mapping, metadata and every indexed document are additionally written here as JSON files (one file per document), so an index can be rebuilt. This slows down indexing considerably (measured: about 26 times on Windows); only use it for indices that have no other source. Indices created with ?archive=false (e.g. by import jobs) are never archived. BackgroundCommitSeconds Optional, default 20. Interval (seconds) in which the server refreshes and commits all open indices in the background. Changes become visible to searches at the latest after this time, even without an explicit refresh. AutoRestoreOnStartup On startup, rebuild archived indices that no longer exist in RootPath (e.g. after a container restart with non-persistent storage). AutoRestoreOnStartupCount If > 0: restore only the last n archived documents per index. AutoRestoreOnStartupSinceSeconds If Count is 0 and this is > 0: restore only documents archived within this period (default 86400 = 1 day). If both are 0, all documents are restored. AllowLegacyGetMutations Default true. Temporarily allows the deprecated GET calls of createindex, removeindex, remove, refresh and releaseall (response carries Deprecation/Warning headers and a warning is logged). If false, these GET calls return 405 Method Not Allowed; only POST/DELETE are accepted. Will default to false in a future version. MaxRequestBodySizeBytes Max. request body size in bytes (e.g. when indexing), applies to Kestrel and IIS. Default 31457280 (30 MB). Larger requests are rejected; index large data sets in several calls. UseHttpsRedirection Default false. If true, HTTP requests are redirected to HTTPS. Only useful if the server itself serves HTTPS (not behind a TLS terminating proxy).

docs.title: API documentation (OpenAPI)
docs.text: Key Description useSwagger true publishes the OpenAPI documents (/openapi/v1.json, /openapi/v2.json) and the API reference UI (Scalar) at /scalar. Always on in Development. The old URLs /swagger and /swagger/{v}/swagger.json redirect to the new ones. These endpoints are accessible without authentication; outside Development a warning is logged at startup.

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text: The Authorization section is described in Authentication.

docs.title: Environment variables
docs.text:
Every setting can be set as an environment variable, using __ as separator:

LUCENESERVER__ROOTPATH=/var/lib/luceneserver/indices
LUCENESERVER__ARCHIVEPATH=/var/lib/luceneserver/archive
AUTHORIZATION__TYPE=Basic
AUTHORIZATION__CLIENTS__0__ID=admin
AUTHORIZATION__CLIENTS__0__SECRETHASH=pbkdf2-sha256$...
AUTHORIZATION__CLIENTS__0__ROLES__0=admin

On Linux, if LUCENESERVER__ROOTPATH is set, no _config/luceneserver.json is created on first start.

docs.title: Index names
docs.text: Index names (and metadata names) must match ^[a-z0-9_-]{1,64}$. Names are lower-cased first. Other names are rejected with success: false.

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text:
By default the server is open: every request is allowed. Set Authorization:Type to Basic to require HTTP Basic authentication.

"Authorization": {
  "Type": "Basic",
  "Clients": [
    {
      "Id": "reader",
      "SecretHash": "pbkdf2-sha256$...",
      "Roles": [ "read" ]
    },
    {
      "Id": "importer",
      "SecretHash": "pbkdf2-sha256$...",
      "Roles": [ "write" ]
    },
    {
      "Id": "admin",
      "SecretHash": "pbkdf2-sha256$...",
      "Roles": [ "admin" ]
    }
  ]
}

Warning

Basic authentication sends credentials with every request. Always use HTTPS.

docs.title: Secrets
docs.text:
Store hashed secrets (SecretHash). Create a hash with:

dotnet LuceneServerNET.dll --hash-secret "my-secret"

The command prints the hash and exits. Plain text secrets (Secret) are still supported for backward compatibility; the server logs a warning on startup.

docs.title: Roles
docs.text:
Role Allowed read search, searchphonetic, group, indexexists, mapping, getmeta, getmetas, getmetanames, /info write read + createindex, map, index, remove, refresh, addmeta admin write + removeindex, releaseall

Higher roles include lower ones. A client without roles gets admin (backward compatible); the server logs a warning. If Basic is enabled but no clients are configured, all requests are rejected.

docs.title: Calling the server
docs.text:
curl -u reader:my-secret "https://search.example.com/Lucene/search/products?q=bat*"

The .NET client accepts the credentials as constructor parameters or in the URL (https://id:secret@host).

docs.title: Installation
docs.text: LuceneServer.NET is an ASP.NET Core application (.NET 10). There are no prebuilt binaries yet, so the server is built from source, as a Docker image or with the NUKE build (ZIP files, see Operations).

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• .NET 10 SDK to build, the ASP.NET Core 10 runtime to run
  • Windows or Linux
  • A directory for the index files (see RootPath)

docs.title: Build
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/jugstalt/LuceneServerNET.git
cd LuceneServerNET
dotnet publish src/LuceneServerNET -c Release -o ./publish

docs.title: First start
docs.text:
cd publish
dotnet LuceneServerNET.dll

On the first start the server creates _config/luceneserver.json from the template _config/proto/_luceneserver.json and prints it to the console. Adjust this file for your environment, see Configuration.

  • Windows: the index directory defaults to a data folder a few levels above the application.
  • Linux: the data directory is taken from the environment variable LUCENESERVER_DATA_PATH (default /etc/luceneserver/data). If LUCENESERVER__ROOTPATH is set, no config file is created and the settings are read from environment variables only.

docs.title: Ports
docs.text:
By default the usual ASP.NET Core settings apply (ASPNETCORE_URLS, --urls). For quick tests the server also accepts:

dotnet LuceneServerNET.dll -expose-http 5000
dotnet LuceneServerNET.dll -expose-https 5001

Note

-expose-http / -expose-https bind to localhost only. Use ASPNETCORE_URLS (e.g. http://0.0.0.0:5000) to listen on all interfaces.

Check that the server runs:

curl http://localhost:5000/info

docs.title: IIS (Windows)
docs.text: The publish output contains a web.config. Install the ASP.NET Core Hosting Bundle, create a website or application pointing to the publish folder and use an application pool with No Managed Code. The application pool identity needs write access to RootPath (and ArchivePath).

docs.title: systemd (Linux)
docs.text:
# /etc/systemd/system/luceneserver.service
[Unit]
Description=LuceneServer.NET
After=network.target

[Service]
WorkingDirectory=/opt/luceneserver
ExecStart=/usr/bin/dotnet /opt/luceneserver/LuceneServerNET.dll
Environment=ASPNETCORE_URLS=http://0.0.0.0:5000
Environment=LUCENESERVER_DATA_PATH=/var/lib/luceneserver
Restart=always
User=luceneserver

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target

sudo systemctl enable --now luceneserver

docs.title: Windows service
docs.text: The server does not register itself as a Windows service. On Windows, hosting in IIS is recommended.

docs.title: Docker
docs.text: See Docker.

docs.title: API documentation
docs.text: With "useSwagger": true (or in the Development environment) the API reference UI (Scalar) is available at /scalar, the OpenAPI documents at /openapi/v1.json and /openapi/v2.json. /swagger redirects to /scalar.

docs.title: Docker
docs.text: The image ghcr.io/jugstalt/luceneserver-net is based on the ASP.NET Core 11 Alpine runtime image and runs the server as the non-root user app. The NUKE build publishes the server and copies it into the image (deploy/docker/server/Dockerfile); releases push it to the GitHub Container Registry.

docs.title: Get or build the image
docs.text:
docker pull ghcr.io/jugstalt/luceneserver-net

Or build it locally (tags {version} and latest; --container-cli wslc or podman instead of Docker):

./build.cmd DockerBuild

docs.title: Run
docs.text:
docker run -d --name luceneserver -p 8080:8080 -v luceneserver-data:/data ghcr.io/jugstalt/luceneserver-net

The server listens on port 8080 inside the container.

docs.title: Volumes
docs.text:
Path in the container Setting Content /data/indices LuceneServer:RootPath the Lucene indices /data/archive LuceneServer:ArchivePath optional, not set by default: the archive (-e LuceneServer__ArchivePath=/data/archive), see Configuration

Mount a volume (or a host directory) on /data. A host directory must be writable for the user app (uid 1654).

One writing instance per index

A Lucene index may only be written by one process. Lucene protects an index with a write.lock file; a second container on the same volume fails with lock errors or, on network file systems with unreliable locks, can corrupt the index. Do not scale the server by starting several replicas on one shared volume. Run one instance per volume.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
The image needs no config file: every setting is read from environment variables (: becomes __, see Configuration).

docker run -d -p 8080:8080 -v luceneserver-data:/data \
  -e Authorization__Type=basic \
  -e Authorization__Clients__0__Id=admin \
  -e Authorization__Clients__0__SecretHash='<hash>' \
  -e Authorization__Clients__0__Roles__0=admin \
  ghcr.io/jugstalt/luceneserver-net

Create the hash with docker run --rm ghcr.io/jugstalt/luceneserver-net --hash-secret <secret>.

Defaults set by the image:

Variable Value ASPNETCORE_HTTP_PORTS 8080 LUCENESERVER__ROOTPATH /data/indices LUCENESERVER__ARCHIVEPATH /data/archive

docs.title: Docker Compose (server + admin UI)
docs.text:
deploy/docker/docker-compose.yml starts the server (port 8080) with Basic authentication and the admin UI (port 8081), which is connected to the server as instance local.

  1. Copy deploy/docker/.env.example to deploy/docker/.env (ignored by git) and fill in the secrets:

    docker run --rm ghcr.io/jugstalt/luceneserver-net --hash-secret 'client-secret'      # LUCENE_ADMIN_CLIENT_SECRET_HASH
docker run --rm ghcr.io/jugstalt/luceneserver-net-admin --hash-password 'password'   # ADMIN_PASSWORD_HASH

    LUCENE_ADMIN_CLIENT_SECRET is the same client secret in plain text. Keep the hashes in single quotes: they contain $.

  2. Start:

    docker compose -f deploy/docker/docker-compose.yml up -d

LUCENE_TAG selects the image version (default latest). Images built locally with --container-cli wslc are not visible to Docker Compose.

docs.title: Health check
docs.text: The image has a Docker HEALTHCHECK on /health; docker ps shows the container as healthy once the index directories are writable.

docs.title: GitHub Container Registry
docs.text:
Releases (git tag v*) push ghcr.io/jugstalt/luceneserver-net:{version}, :{major.minor} and :latest from the GitHub workflow release.yml; pre-releases only get :{version}. To push from your machine, log in with a token that has the write:packages scope and run ./build.cmd DockerPush:

docker login ghcr.io -u <user>

docs.title: Health endpoints
docs.text:
Endpoint Checks Use /health the process answers and RootPath (and ArchivePath, if set) exists and is writable readiness probe, load balancer, Docker HEALTHCHECK /alive the process answers liveness probe

Both answer 200 Healthy or 503 Unhealthy as plain text, without details (no paths, no exception messages). They need no authentication, also with Authorization:Type = basic: probes of Docker, Kubernetes or a load balancer send no credentials.

docs.title: Metrics and traces (OpenTelemetry)
docs.text:
The server records logs, metrics and traces with OpenTelemetry. They are exported via OTLP as soon as OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT is set (e.g. an OpenTelemetry Collector, the Aspire dashboard, Grafana Alloy):

OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT=http://otel-collector:4317
OTEL_SERVICE_NAME=luceneserver

Besides the ASP.NET Core and .NET runtime metrics (e.g. http.server.request.duration per route) the meter LuceneServerNET provides:

Metric Type Tags luceneserver.search.duration histogram (s) index, operation (search, phonetic, groupby) luceneserver.search.requests counter index, operation, outcome (success, error) luceneserver.documents.indexed counter index

docs.title: Scaling
docs.text:
One writing instance per index

A Lucene index may only be written by one process at a time (write.lock). Run exactly one server per index directory; don't share an index directory between several instances, containers or replicas.

docs.title: Local development with Aspire
docs.text:
src/aspire/LuceneServerNET.AppHost starts the server together with the Aspire dashboard (logs, traces, metrics); the index data goes to artifacts/aspire-data:

dotnet run --project src/aspire/LuceneServerNET.AppHost

Further web apps (e.g. an admin UI) are added to the AppHost and reference the server.

docs.title: Build and deploy (NUKE)
docs.text:
Command Result ./build.cmd build and test ./build.cmd PrintVersion the version (MinVer, from the git tags v*) ./build.cmd Test Pack Zip NuGet packages in artifacts/packages, ZIP files artifacts/zip/luceneserver_net_{version}_{win-x64\|linux-x64}.zip (framework dependent) ./build.cmd DockerBuild [--container-cli wslc\|podman] images ghcr.io/jugstalt/luceneserver-net and ghcr.io/jugstalt/luceneserver-net-admin ({version}, {major.minor}, latest) ./build.cmd Docs this documentation in artifacts/docs/site ./build.cmd DocsPublish [--docs-repository <path>] copies the site to docs-gviewonline/app/other/luceneserver-net (nothing is committed)

The version comes from the git tags (v3.0.0, v3.1.0-preview.1, ...). Pushing a tag runs the GitHub workflow release.yml: it publishes the NuGet packages (LuceneServerNET.Core, LuceneServerNET.Client), pushes the images to ghcr.io/jugstalt and creates the GitHub release with the ZIP files. The release notes are the section of the version in CHANGELOG.md.

docs.title: LuceneServer.NET
docs.text:
LuceneServer.NET ist ein REST-Server auf Basis von Apache Lucene.NET. Er verwaltet beliebig viele Suchindizes und stellt sie über einfache GET/POST-Requests bereit.

  • Umgesetzt in C# auf .NET 10
  • Volltextsuche mit Lucene-Query-Syntax
  • Phonetische Suche (Soundex, Kölner Phonetik)
  • Geo-Filter (Bounding Box, Distanz, Distanz zu einer Linie) und Ausgabe als GeoJSON
  • Gruppierung (ähnlich DISTINCT) von Feldwerten
  • Optionale Basic-Authentifizierung mit Rollen (read, write, admin)
  • .NET-Client-Bibliothek LuceneServerNET.Client
  • Kommandozeilen-Tools zum Befüllen eines Index aus bestehenden Datenbanken

docs.title: Motivation
docs.text:
Ziel ist eine schnelle und einfache Suche. Die Performance soll hoch genug sein, um auch in großen Datenmengen in Echtzeit aus Autocomplete-Eingabefeldern zu suchen.

Typische Anwendungsfälle:

  • Suchen in Produktlisten
  • Suchen in großen Geodatenbeständen wie Adressen, Grundstücken usw.
  • Indizieren von Dokumenten

Der Suchindex dient in erster Linie dem schnellen Auffinden. Über die Treffer wird auf die eigentlichen Daten verlinkt. Er ist kein Ersatz für eine Datenbank, sondern sorgt für eine performante und bedienbare Suche. Mit den enthaltenen Tools kann ein Index aus bestehenden (relationalen) Datenbanken befüllt werden, z. B. regelmäßig; über im Index gespeicherte Datenbankschlüssel gelangt man zurück zum Originaldatensatz.

docs.title: Weiterlesen
docs.text: Installation Server bauen, starten und hosten Konfiguration Indexpfade, Wiederherstellung, API-Dokumentation Authentifizierung Clients, Secrets und Rollen REST-API Alle Endpunkte .NET-Client Server aus C# verwenden

docs.title: Admin-Oberfläche
docs.text: LuceneServerNET.Admin ist eine eigene Webanwendung (Blazor Server, MudBlazor), mit der eine oder mehrere LuceneServer.NET-Instanzen administriert werden. Sie spricht die Server ausschließlich über die REST-API v2 an und kann daher überall laufen, wo die Server erreichbar sind.

docs.title: Funktionen
docs.text:
Bereich Möglichkeiten Dashboard Health, Version, Uptime, Speicher und Anzahl der Indizes jeder Instanz, Rollen des API-Clients Instanzen Instanzen anlegen, bearbeiten, entfernen und testen (zusätzlich zu denen aus der Konfiguration) Indizes Liste mit Dokumentanzahl, Größe auf der Platte und letzter Änderung; filtern und sortieren Suche Autocomplete-Eingabe (Search as you type, jedes Wort ist ein Pflicht-Präfix: graz haupt → +graz* +haupt*), Suche mit size/from/searchAfter, Sortierung, räumlicher Filter, phonetische Suche, Gruppierung, Ergebnis als Tabelle oder JSON, Request als curl-Befehl Index anlegen Mapping-Editor: Felder, Typen, indiziert/gespeichert, Primärfelder, Phonetik Datenbank-Verbindungen SQL Server-, PostgreSQL- und SQLite-Verbindungen als Importquelle (verschlüsselt gespeichert), Verbindungstest (auch in der Liste); Show connection string zeigt den gespeicherten String mit maskiertem Passwort (Audit-Log connection.show), ein belassenes ***** behält das gespeicherte Passwort Import Aus einer Datenbank-Abfrage oder CSV, JSON bzw. GeoJSON (inkl. Geodaten) (Array oder NDJSON) hochladen, Vorschau, Mapping aus den ersten 200 Zeilen vorgeschlagen (neuer Index) bzw. Spalten dem bestehenden Mapping zugeordnet, einstellbare Batchgröße, Abbruch, Fehlerreport Metadaten Eigene Metadaten anzeigen und bearbeiten Import-Jobs Wiederkehrende Importe aus einer Datenbank-Abfrage (Cron-Zeitplan): neu aufbauen und Alias umschalten, leeren und neu befüllen oder anhängen; Lauf-Verlauf Audit-Log Wer wann was geändert hat (Index, Metadaten, Import, Instanzen, Verbindungen, Logins), mit Filtern; Aufbewahrung Admin:Audit:RetentionDays (Standard 180) Aliases Index-Aliases anlegen, umschalten und entfernen (siehe API v2); Aliases stehen in der Indexliste; ein Klick auf einen Alias öffnet seine Seite: Suche, curl-Befehl, Kopieren und Backup verwenden den Alias-Namen (immer die aktuelle Generation); Wartung und Import nur direkt am Index Backup / Restore Index als ZIP herunterladen (Backup auf der Index-Seite) und auf einer beliebigen Instanz wiederherstellen (Restore in der Indexliste) Kopieren Index (Mapping, Metadaten, Dokumente) unter neuem Namen auf derselben oder auf eine andere Instanz kopieren Wartung Refresh, Dokumente per Query löschen, Index leeren, Index löschen (Rolle admin, Bestätigung per Name)

Die Oberfläche bietet nur an, was der API-Client der Instanz darf: Sie fragt den Server (GET /api/v2/admin/whoami) nach den Rollen read, write und admin.

docs.title: Starten
docs.text:
AspiredotnetDocker

Der AppHost startet Server und Admin-Oberfläche:

dotnet run --project src/aspire/LuceneServerNET.AppHost

Login admin / admin (Parameter admin-password, in den User Secrets des AppHost änderbar).

dotnet run --project src/LuceneServerNET.Admin

./build.cmd DockerBuild   # oder: docker pull ghcr.io/jugstalt/luceneserver-net-admin
docker run --rm ghcr.io/jugstalt/luceneserver-net-admin --hash-password "mein passwort"
docker run -p 8081:8080 -v luceneserver-admin-data:/data \
  -e Admin__Authentication__Users__0__Name=admin \
  -e Admin__Authentication__Users__0__PasswordHash='pbkdf2-sha256$...' \
  -e Admin__Instances__0__Name=prod \
  -e Admin__Instances__0__Url=http://luceneserver:8080 \
  ghcr.io/jugstalt/luceneserver-net-admin

docs.title: Als Windows-Dienst betreiben
docs.text:
Das Release-ZIP (luceneserver-net-win64-{version}.zip) enthält die Admin-Oberfläche in {version}/admin und zwei Skripte im Versionsordner:

Skript Zweck lucene-admin.bat startet die Admin-Oberfläche in einer Konsole (http://localhost:5180) lucene-admin-service.bat installiert sie als Windows-Dienst

Import-Jobs laufen nur, solange die Anwendung läuft. Ein Windows-Dienst startet mit dem Server und wird nach einem Absturz neu gestartet; unter Windows ist das daher der empfohlene Weg. Das Skript in einer Eingabeaufforderung als Administrator ausführen:

lucene-admin-service.bat install [name] [port]
lucene-admin-service.bat uninstall [name]

install legt den Dienst an und startet ihn:

  • Dienstname lucene-admin, mit Namen lucene-admin-<name>. Er startet automatisch (verzögert) und wird nach einem Absturz neu gestartet.
  • Er hört auf http://localhost:<port> (Standard 5180). Für den Zugriff von anderen Rechnern einen Reverse Proxy (IIS mit ARR, nginx, ...) mit HTTPS davorsetzen.
  • Er läuft unter dem virtuellen Konto NT SERVICE\lucene-admin[-<name>], das nur in admin-data schreiben und _config lesen darf.
  • Neben den Versionsordnern (überleben Updates): admin-data (SQLite-Datenbank admin.db, Data-Protection-Schlüssel) und _config\admin.json. Bei der ersten Installation legt das Skript admin.json mit leerer Benutzerliste an: einen Benutzer (admin\LuceneServerNET.Admin.exe --hash-password <passwort>) und Instanzen eintragen, dann den Dienst neu starten. admin.json überschreibt appsettings.json; Umgebungsvariablen überschreiben admin.json.
D:\lucene-admin\
  3.0.0\                          Versionsordner aus dem ZIP
    admin\                        Anwendung
    lucene-admin-service.bat
  admin-data\                     admin.db, keys
  _config\admin.json              Konfiguration

Mehrere Instanzen auf einem Server: ein Stammordner pro Instanz, jeweils mit eigenem Namen und Port. install verweigert einen Namen, dessen Dienst zu einem anderen Stammordner gehört.

Update: die neue Version in denselben Stammordner entpacken und ihr lucene-admin-service.bat install mit gleichem Namen und Port ausführen. Das Skript stoppt den Dienst, stellt ihn auf die neue Version um und startet ihn wieder (Datenbank-Migrationen laufen beim Start). Zurück geht es mit install der alten Version (nur, wenn die neue Version die Datenbank nicht migriert hat).

Eigenes Konto: für SQL Server mit Windows-Authentifizierung braucht das virtuelle Konto einen Login am SQL Server (NT SERVICE\lucene-admin), oder in den Diensteigenschaften (Reiter Anmelden) ein Domänenkonto eintragen und ihm dieselben Rechte geben.

Warnungen und Fehler gehen ins Windows-Ereignisprotokoll (Anwendungsprotokoll, Quelle LuceneServer.NET Admin).

docs.title: IIS
docs.text:
Die Admin-Oberfläche läuft auch im IIS (ASP.NET Core Hosting Bundle, In-Process). IIS startet die Anwendung erst mit der ersten Anfrage und recycelt sie (Leerlauf-Timeout, standardmäßig alle 29 Stunden); geplante Import-Jobs laufen im IIS daher nicht verlässlich. Entweder:

  • die Oberfläche im IIS mit Admin:Jobs:Enabled = false betreiben und zusätzlich den Windows-Dienst auf demselben DataPath (er führt die Jobs aus; gleiche Data-Protection-Schlüssel, beide können die gespeicherten Secrets entschlüsseln), oder
  • den Anwendungspool einstellen: Startmodus AlwaysRunning, Leerlauf-Timeout 0, kein periodisches Recycling, und Vorabladen aktiviert true an der Site (Feature Anwendungsinitialisierung). Verpasste Läufe werden nach einem Recycle nachgeholt (Catch up missed runs).

Die Identität des Anwendungspools braucht Schreibrechte auf DataPath. Blazor Server braucht WebSockets (IIS-Feature WebSocket-Protokoll).

docs.title: Konfiguration
docs.text:
{
  "Admin": {
    "DataPath": "_data",            // SQLite-Datenbank (admin.db) + Data-Protection-Schlüssel
    "PublicUrl": "https://admin.example.com",  // optional: Links in Job-Webhooks
    "Import": { "MaxFileSizeMB": 500, "CommandTimeoutSeconds": 600 },
    "Audit": { "RetentionDays": 180 },
    "Jobs": { "Enabled": true },    // false: keine geplanten Läufe (z. B. eine zweite Admin-Instanz auf derselben Datenbank)
    "Authentication": {
      "Type": "Local",              // Local | Oidc | None (None: kein Login, nur lokale Entwicklung!)
      "Users": [
        { "Name": "admin", "PasswordHash": "pbkdf2-sha256$..." }
      ],
      "Oidc": {
        "Authority": "https://login.example.com/realms/main",
        "ClientId": "lucene-admin",
        "ClientSecret": "...",
        "Scopes": [ "openid", "profile" ],
        "RequiredRole": "lucene-admin"   // optional, Rollen-Claim "roles"
      }
    },
    "Instances": [
      { "Name": "prod", "Url": "https://lucene.example.com", "ClientId": "admin-ui", "ClientSecret": "..." }
    ]
  }
}
  • Passwort-Hashes: LuceneServerNET.Admin --hash-password <passwort> (gleiches Format wie --hash-secret des Servers). Ein Klartext-Password funktioniert ebenfalls, erzeugt aber eine Warnung im Log.
  • Konfigurationsdatei außerhalb des Anwendungsordners: die Umgebungsvariable LUCENE_ADMIN_CONFIG=<pfad>dmin.json lädt eine zusätzliche Datei, die appsettings.json überschreibt (verwenden die Windows-Dienst-Skripte).
  • Instanzen aus der Konfiguration sind in der Oberfläche schreibgeschützt. In der Oberfläche angelegte Instanzen liegen in admin.db; ihre Client-Secrets werden mit ASP.NET Core Data Protection verschlüsselt (Schlüssel in DataPath/keys). DataPath muss auf einem persistenten Volume liegen, sonst lassen sich gespeicherte Secrets nach einem Neustart nicht mehr entschlüsseln.
  • API-Client pro Instanz: Am Server einen Client anlegen (siehe Authentifizierung), mit der Rolle, die in der Oberfläche erlaubt sein soll, z. B. admin für volle Administration oder read nur für die Suche.

Warning

Wer sich an der Admin-Oberfläche anmelden kann, darf auf allen Instanzen alles, was die konfigurierten API-Clients dürfen. Nicht ohne OIDC oder starke Passwörter öffentlich erreichbar machen und HTTPS verwenden.

docs.title: Import
docs.text:
1. Bestehenden Index auswählen oder den Namen eines neuen Index eingeben.
  2. Datei: CSV-Datei (Kopfzeile, Trennzeichen , ; Tab oder | wird erkannt) oder JSON (Array von Objekten, { "items": [...] } oder NDJSON) hochladen. Datenbank: Verbindung wählen (Menü Database connections), SELECT-Abfrage eingeben und Preview klicken. Der Indexname wird aus der Tabelle nach FROM übernommen.
  3. Vorgeschlagenes Mapping prüfen. Regeln: Ganzzahlen → int32, Zahlen → double, ISO-Datum → datetime, kurze Werte ohne Leerzeichen → string, alles andere → text. Spalten lat/lon (auch latitude/longitude, lng) werden zusätzlich zu einem geo-Feld location kombiniert. Textfelder werden Primärfelder. Feldnamen dürfen nicht mit _ beginnen.
  4. Batchgröße wählen (Dokumente pro Request, Standard 500) und starten. Zeilen, die nicht zum Mapping passen, werden übersprungen und im Report aufgelistet; lehnt der Server einen Batch ab, werden dessen Dokumente einzeln gesendet, um die fehlerhaften Zeilen zu finden. Am Ende wird der Index einmal refresht.

docs.title: Import aus einer Datenbank
docs.text:
• Provider: SQL Server (Microsoft.Data.SqlClient), PostgreSQL (Npgsql), SQLite (Microsoft.Data.Sqlite).
  • Erlaubt ist nur eine einzelne SELECT-Anweisung (oder WITH ... SELECT). Sie läuft in einer Transaktion, die immer zurückgerollt wird. Das ist ein Sicherheitsnetz, kein Berechtigungskonzept: einen Datenbank-User mit reinen Leserechten verwenden.
  • Die Abfrage läuft zweimal: für die Vorschau (erste 200 Zeilen) und für den Import (gestreamt, alle Zeilen). Gleichnamige Spalten bekommen ein Suffix (id, id2), Binärspalten werden übersprungen, decimal wird zu double.
  • Timeout pro Abfrage: Admin:Import:CommandTimeoutSeconds (Standard 600).

docs.title: Geodaten
docs.text:
Quelle Erkannt als Spalten lat/lon (auch latitude/longitude, lng) Punkt, EPSG:4326 Spalten x/y (auch rechtswert/hochwert, easting/northing) Punkt, der EPSG-Code muss gewählt werden Geometrie-Spalte: WKB/EWKB (Bytes), WKT/EWKT (SRID=31256;POLYGON(...)), GeoJSON-Geometrie Punkt, Linie, Polygon (auch Multi) GeoJSON-Datei (.geojson, FeatureCollection) properties werden Felder, geometry eine Geometrie-Spalte, id das Feld id

Weitere Koordinatenspalten lassen sich im Mapping hinzufügen (Add point from columns).

  • Koordinatensystem: Eine SRID im Wert (EWKB, EWKT, GeoJSON crs) hat Vorrang, sonst gilt der EPSG-Code des Geo-Felds (Standard 4326). Alles wird mit Proj4Net.Core nach WGS84 umgerechnet; unbekannte EPSG-Codes werden vor dem Import gemeldet.
  • Linien und Polygone: Der Server indiziert Punkte, das geo-Feld bekommt daher den Point on Surface (liegt immer auf der Linie bzw. im Polygon, berechnet mit SpatialNET im Quellsystem). Die Bounding-Box steht in <feld>_bbox als "minx,miny,maxx,maxy" (WGS84, nicht indiziert); Punkte bekommen keine.
  • Template-Felder (Add template field): ein Feld aus mehreren Spalten, z. B. {PLZ} {ORT} {STR} {HNR} oder Adresse in {ORT} ({ORTSTEIL}). Spaltennamen ohne Groß-/Kleinschreibung, NULL ist leer, Zahlen kulturunabhängig (12.5), Datum ISO; mehrfache Leerzeichen werden zusammengefasst und leere Klammern () / [] entfernt. Replacements (von → nach) gelten für alle Template-Felder.
  • Original-Geometrie (optional, standardmäßig aus): <feld>_geojson, GeoJSON in WGS84 mit 7 Nachkommastellen (RFC 7946).
  • Datenbanken: PostGIS-Spalten geometry / geography werden direkt gelesen (als EWKB mit SRID, auch bei SELECT *). SQL-Server-Geometrietypen als WKB abfragen:
-- PostGIS: direkt, oder ausdrücklich als EWKB (behält die SRID)
SELECT id, name, geom FROM places
SELECT id, name, ST_AsEWKB(geom) AS geom FROM places
-- SQL Server geometry / geography (EPSG-Code im Mapping wählen)
SELECT id, name, geom.STAsBinary() AS geom FROM places

Gesucht wird mit dem räumlichen Filter auf das Geo-Feld, z. B. dist_km(geom:15.44,47.07,5) oder bbox(geom:15.4,47.0,15.5,47.1).

docs.title: Kopieren
docs.text: Copy auf der Index-Seite kopiert Mapping, Metadaten und alle Dokumente unter einen neuen Indexnamen oder auf eine andere Instanz (der API-Client des Ziels braucht die Rolle write). Die Dokumente kommen aus GET /api/v2/indices/{id}/documents/_export, der nur gespeicherte Felder liefert: Felder mit "store": false gehen beim Kopieren verloren (die Seite zeigt sie vorher an). Ein bestehendes Ziel wird nur mit Replace the target if it exists überschrieben.

docs.title: Import-Jobs
docs.text:
Import jobs führen Datenbank-Abfragen (eine oder mehrere Quellen) nach Zeitplan, manuell oder von außen ausgelöst aus und importieren das Ergebnis. Das Mapping wird einmal über die Vorschau erkannt, kann angepasst werden und wird mit dem Job gespeichert (die Spalten der Abfragen dürfen sich danach nicht ändern).

Modus Ablauf Neu aufbauen und Alias umschalten Ein neuer Index {alias}_{yyyyMMddHHmmss} wird angelegt (ohne Archiv, er wird bei jedem Lauf neu aufgebaut) und befüllt; bei Erfolg wird der Alias umgeschaltet und ältere Generationen werden gelöscht, bis auf die neuesten Keep older generations (Standard 1, für ein Rollback über die Alias-Seite). Generationen, auf die irgendein Alias zeigt, werden nie gelöscht. Schlägt der Lauf fehl, wird die neue Generation entfernt und der Alias bleibt unverändert. Clients verwenden den Alias-Namen. Leeren und neu befüllen Der Index wird geleert und neu befüllt (Suchen sehen währenddessen einen leeren bzw. halben Index). Anhängen Dokumente werden hinzugefügt.
  • Zeitplan: Cron-Ausdruck mit 5 Feldern (Minute Stunde Tag Monat Wochentag, z. B. 0 3 * * *) und Zeitzone (leer = UTC). Die Seite zeigt die nächsten Läufe. Ohne Cron-Ausdruck (manual) läuft der Job nur über Run now.
  • Fortschritt eines laufenden Jobs (Job-Liste und Job-Seite): gelesene Zeilen, Rate und Laufzeit; ab dem zweiten Lauf ein Prozentwert, geschätzt aus der Zeilenzahl des letzten erfolgreichen Laufs.
  • Dry run (Job-Seite): liest und konvertiert alle Zeilen wie ein Lauf, schickt aber nichts (kein Index, keine Metadaten, kein Alias). Jeder Lauf zeigt, wo die Zeit bleibt: read (Datenbank), convert (Templates, Geometrie) und send (Server).
  • Jetzt ausführen, Abbrechen und ein Lauf-Verlauf (Status, Dauer, Zahlen, Index, Meldung) pro Job. Jeder Lauf steht im Audit-Log.
  • Externer Auslöser: den Job von außen starten statt (oder zusätzlich zu) einem Zeitplan, z. B. am Ende eines Jenkins-Jobs, der die Datenbank aktualisiert. Siehe Import-Jobs von außen auslösen.
  • Webhook (optional): nach einem Lauf wird die URL mit POST und einem JSON-Body aufgerufen, entweder nur bei Fehlern (failed, cancelled, interrupted; Standard) oder nach jedem Lauf. Ein optionaler Header Name: Wert (z. B. Authorization: Bearer ...) wird verschlüsselt gespeichert. Bis zu 3 Versuche (5 s Abstand, 30 s Timeout); das Ergebnis steht im Lauf-Verlauf, ein fehlschlagender Webhook ändert den Status des Laufs nicht. Test webhook schickt ein Beispiel. Das Feld text ist eine einzeilige Zusammenfassung, die Slack- und Mattermost-Incoming-Webhooks direkt anzeigen:
{
  "text": "❌ Import job orte: failed · prod/orte_20261107030000 · read 10, imported 9, failed 1 · 12.5 s · ...",
  "job": "orte", "jobId": 7, "runId": 3, "instance": "prod", "target": "orte", "mode": "replace_alias",
  "index": "orte_20261107030000", "status": "failed", "success": false, "triggeredBy": "job:orte",
  "startedUtc": "2026-11-07T03:00:00Z", "finishedUtc": "2026-11-07T03:00:12.5Z", "durationSeconds": 12.5,
  "read": 10, "imported": 9, "failed": 1, "message": "...", "url": "https://admin.example.com/jobs/7"
}

status ist succeeded, warning (Zeilen übersprungen), failed, cancelled oder interrupted; url gibt es nur, wenn Admin:PublicUrl konfiguriert ist. - Läufe finden nur statt, solange die Admin-App läuft. Mit Catch up missed runs (Standard an) läuft ein Job beim Start einmal, wenn ein geplanter Lauf verpasst wurde, während die App nicht lief (nur einmal, egal wie viele verpasst wurden). Läufe, die bei einem Herunterfahren aktiv waren, werden als interrupted markiert. Für verlässliche Zeitpläne die Admin-App als Dienst betreiben (siehe Als Windows-Dienst betreiben). Pro Datenbank nur eine Admin-Instanz mit Admin:Jobs:Enabled = true betreiben.

docs.title: Quellen und die webgis-Vorlage
docs.text:
Ein Job hat eine oder mehrere Quellen (Reiter auf der Job-Seite): jeweils mit eigener Datenbank-Verbindung, Abfrage, Mapping und Metadaten. Alle Quellen werden in denselben Index (dieselbe Generation) importiert; bei Neu aufbauen und Alias umschalten wird der Alias nach der letzten Quelle umgeschaltet. Ein Feld, das mehrere Quellen verwenden, muss überall denselben Typ haben. Phonetik und Encode characters gelten für den Index.

Metadaten pro Quelle: im Index unter der Meta-ID der Quelle gespeichert (32 Hex-Zeichen, einmal erzeugt, für jeden Lauf gleich) als JSON {"id", "category", "sample", "description", "service", "query", ...} plus eigene Schlüssel. Im Modus Leeren und neu befüllen werden Einträge von Quellen, die aus dem Job entfernt wurden (Schlüssel im Format einer Meta-ID), gelöscht.

Template-Variablen: {@metaid} (Meta-ID der Quelle) und {@category} (Kategorie aus den Metadaten).

webgis-Vorlage (Apply webgis template nach der Vorschau, ID-Spalte wählen): die Struktur des webgis-Suchindex, die das gView-Werkzeug FillLuceneServer ablöst:

Feld Inhalt id {@metaid}.{ID-Spalte} – webgis liest daraus die Meta-ID, aus den Metadaten Service und Query und das Objekt über seine ID suggested_text Template, z. B. {PLZ} {ORT} {STR} {HNR} (Primärfeld, Pflicht) subtext Template, z. B. Adresse in {ORT} ({ORTSTEIL}) (Primärfeld) category {@category} (Primärfeld; die Kategorie in den Metadaten ist Pflicht) thumbnail_url Template oder feste URL (nur gespeichert) geo, bbox die erste Geo-Quelle (Punkt; Linien und Polygone: Punkt auf der Fläche, bbox in WGS84)

Die übrigen Spalten bleiben im Mapping sichtbar, werden aber nicht importiert. Die ID-Spalte wird vorgeschlagen (objectid, oid, fid, gid, id, sonst die erste Ganzzahl-Spalte). Die Meta-ID bleibt bei jedem Lauf gleich, die Dokument-IDs sind also stabil (gView hat bei jedem Befüllen eine neue erzeugt).

gView-Konfiguration: Import gView configuration auf der Job-Seite legt aus einem gView-FillLuceneServer-JSON einen Job an (eine webgis-Quelle pro Feature-Klasse, SELECT * FROM {name} WHERE {filter}, Templates, Kategorie, Ersetzungen, Metadaten, Phonetik, Encode-Zeichen). Die Connection-Strings der Datei werden nicht verwendet: eine Datenbank-Verbindung wählen.

docs.title: Import-Jobs von außen auslösen
docs.text:
Create trigger token auf der Job-Seite erzeugt ein Token für diesen Job. Es wird nur einmal angezeigt (gespeichert als SHA-256-Hash), darf nur diesen Job starten und kann erneuert oder widerrufen werden. Jeder Aufruf steht im Audit-Log (job.trigger, mit IP-Adresse).

# Jenkins (sh), am Ende des Jobs, der die Datenbank aktualisiert
curl --fail -X POST "https://admin.example.com/api/jobs/7/run" \
     -H "Authorization: Bearer $LUCENE_JOB_TOKEN" \
     -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d "{\"note\":\"jenkins #$BUILD_NUMBER\"}"

rem Jenkins (bat)
curl --fail -X POST "https://admin.example.com/api/jobs/7/run" -H "Authorization: Bearer %LUCENE_JOB_TOKEN%" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d "{\"note\":\"jenkins #%BUILD_NUMBER%\"}"

Das Token in einem Jenkins-Credential (Secret text) ablegen, nicht in der Job-Definition.

Aufruf Antwort POST /api/jobs/{id}/run 202 {"status":"started","runId":12,"statusUrl":"/api/jobs/7/runs/12"}; läuft der Job gerade: 202 {"status":"queued"} – er läuft direkt nach dem aktuellen Lauf noch einmal (mehrere Aufrufe während eines Laufs: ein weiterer Lauf) GET /api/jobs/{id}/runs/{runId} 200 mit status, finished, success, Zeiten, Zahlen, message, note, webhook Job oder Token ungültig 401 Job deaktiviert 409
  • Das Token geht als Authorization: Bearer <token> mit (oder im Header X-Job-Token). Die optionale note (JSON-Body oder ?note=, max. 200 Zeichen) steht im Lauf-Verlauf und wird mit dem Webhook geschickt.
  • Der Aufruf kehrt sofort zurück. Soll der Jenkins-Build bei einem fehlgeschlagenen Import fehlschlagen, die statusUrl abfragen, bis finished true ist, und success prüfen; für Benachrichtigungen reicht meist der Webhook des Jobs.
  • Ein Zeitplan kann als Sicherheitsnetz bleiben (z. B. 0 6 * * *): er läuft unabhängig vom Auslöser.
  • Die Admin-Oberfläche muss von Jenkins aus erreichbar sein (HTTPS, siehe Als Windows-Dienst betreiben / IIS).

docs.title: Backup und Restore
docs.text:
Backup auf der Index-Seite lädt ein ZIP herunter:

Datei Inhalt manifest.json Format, Index, Instanz, Server-Version, Zeitpunkt, Anzahl Dokumente, nicht gespeicherte Felder mapping.json das Mapping metadata.json die eigenen Metadaten documents.ndjson alle Dokumente (gespeicherte Felder, ein JSON-Objekt pro Zeile)

Restore in der Indexliste lädt so ein ZIP hoch (max. Admin:Import:MaxFileSizeMB) und legt den Index unter dem ursprünglichen oder einem anderen Namen an, auf einer beliebigen Instanz; ein bestehender Index wird nur mit Replace the target if it exists ersetzt. Wie beim Kopieren enthält ein Backup nur gespeicherte Felder. Für eine vollständige, laufende Sicherung dient das Archiv des Servers (LuceneServer:ArchivePath).

docs.title: REST-API v2
docs.text:
Die API v2 ist ressourcenorientiert und liegt unter /api/v2/indices. Sie läuft parallel zur API v1 (/Lucene/...): Beide arbeiten auf denselben Indizes mit derselben Engine, bestehende v1-Clients funktionieren unverändert weiter. v1 gilt als deprecated; neue Clients sollten v2 verwenden.

Antworten, Rollen, Query-Syntax, outFields-Funktionen, Geo-Filter und format sind wie in v1. Jede Version hat ein eigenes OpenAPI-Dokument (/openapi/v1.json, /openapi/v2.json); die API-Referenz-UI (/scalar) zeigt beide.

docs.title: Fehler und HTTP-Statuscodes
docs.text:
Anders als v1 (immer HTTP 200) liefert v2 Fehler mit passendem Statuscode. Der Body ist in beiden Fällen gleich:

{ "success": false, "message": "Cannot parse 'title:(': ..." }
Status Ursache 400 Ungültige Query (Lucene-Syntax), ungültiger Geo-Filter, ungültige Parameter (z. B. from + size > 10000, ungültiger Index-Name) 404 Index existiert nicht 409 Index existiert bereits bzw. wird gerade entladen 413 Request-Body zu groß (LuceneServer:MaxRequestBodySizeBytes) 500 Sonstige Fehler (Meldung außerhalb von Development nur mit Fehlertyp)

docs.text:
